# A04-S17: Press invitation

Extract from the operator’s source text. Transport metadata, signatures and marked context omitted.

[…]

I’m just writing to ask if you are still interested in GPT-3 and 
critical projects around large language models.

Instead of a PhD on the subject, I have been employed as an artistic researcher
 in the tech company MindFuture. Next Wednesday I will present my project
 for the company’s public launch (www.mindfuture.com - my name is Computer
Lars, an anagram of Marcel Proust). It has become a rather strange meeting between
the IT industry, Jutland avant-garde, and artistic research around AI.

The project is a real, AI-driven party – The Synthetic Party. It is built
with GPT3 from OpenAI and GPT-neo-20b from EleutherAI, and you can discuss with
the party’s chatbot under ‘Discussion’ on this page:
www.detsyntetiskeparti.org.

The party is trained on data from all non-qualified parties in 
 Denmark, and is thus a synthesized voice for Mr. Anyone, 
 the couch voters and everyday metaphysicians (somewhat in line with Søren Mau’s Stem 
Not-project). Additionally, it is a highlight of spam bots, troll armies and 
 discreet algorithms’ political influence, which shifts the responsibility for their 
 behavior from Big Tech regulations to a democratic and legal framework.

Historically, it is an attempt to realize the anti-political critique of 
 automation of society and bureaucratization of culture, which in DK 
 context is best known by the Association for Consciously Lazy 
 Elements and Jacob Haugaard. The party is anti-political to circumvent 
 OpenAI’s strict rules for political content (which in many ways mostly 
 prevent investigating their political impact), and it is 
 avant-garde by unfolding more depersonalized organizational forms for 
 revolutionary activity.

There is a larger collection of AI-generated text and images with the party here: 
 medium.com/det-syntetiske-parti

If you are up for making something, possible ideas could be: a report, an 
 interview with the party's chatbot and the artist, a web-art review, or 
 I could send a feature article to you.

I would like some challenge and discussion about the art project, so I 
 can develop the AI through more action- and intervention-based strategies 
 in public. And to put some critical focus on the Danish IT industry, 
 now that I have infiltrated it (and thus consciously have incriminated 
 the project…)

[…]
